# namesilo_domain_lock (Resource)

Manages one domain's registrar lock — the lock that prevents unauthorized transfers of the domain to another registrar.

`locked` is the desired state, so resource existence does not imply the domain is locked: `locked = false` keeps this resource and declares that the domain must be unlocked, rather than deleting the resource to unlock it. Destroy unlocks the domain only when the state says it was locked — removing the resource releases the lock, and unlocking a domain removes the main safeguard against an unauthorized transfer.

Some registry states reject both locking and unlocking (a pending transfer, for example); when that happens the API error is surfaced unchanged, so the registry's own message is what you see. Drift detection is the normal refresh: a change made in the web UI is picked up on the next plan and corrected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "namesilo_domain_lock" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
  locked = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain whose registrar lock to manage, e.g. `example.com`. Changing it forces a replacement: the resource is pointed at a different domain rather than renamed. Also the import ID.
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether the domain is locked against transfer at the registrar. This is the desired state, not a claim about the current one: `locked = false` keeps the resource and keeps the domain unlocked. Unlocking a domain removes the main safeguard against an unauthorized transfer.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The domain name. It is inert (Terraform keys state by resource address), it makes `tofu state show` readable, and it is the import ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the domain name. Import seeds domain and id, then the
# refresh that follows reads the registrar lock from the API and stores the
# locked flag.
tofu import namesilo_domain_lock.example example.com
```
